facts.advisory_summary: Double flow control refund on HTTP/2 server streams in net/http — The HTTP/2 server can refund connection-level flow control twice for the same data: Once when a client resets a stream (refunding data for any sent-but-unread portion of the stream), and again when a request handler reads the buffered data. Total buffered data is still limited by the concurrent stream limit and stream-level flow control.

facts.advisory_summary: HTTP/2 server crash due to HPACK encoder race in net/http — HTTP/2 servers could end up crashing due to inadvertently modifying its HPACK encoder concurrently. A malicious client can repeatedly send a request while changing the header table size to crash the server.
